desc:
Bugs cost you users, support time and trust. Ecom Swift LLC offers SaaS bug fixing and issue triage for web apps: we reproduce each problem, find its cause, fix it on a branch in your repository and test that it stays fixed.

## What is SaaS bug fixing and issue triage?

SaaS bug fixing is the work of finding why your product behaves differently from what users expect, then correcting it without breaking something else. Issue triage is the step before that: sorting a pile of reports by how many people they affect and how risky they are, so the right problems get fixed first.

Most teams have a list of known bugs that never quite reaches the top of the sprint. Each item looks small. Together they create a product that feels unreliable, and every new feature has to be built on top of them.

## Why open bugs get expensive

A bug rarely stays the size it was when it was reported. Users work around it, then build habits around the workaround. Support staff write saved replies for it. Developers learn which screens to avoid. Months later nobody remembers what the correct behavior was supposed to be.

Fixing a bug early is cheaper than fixing it late, because the cause is still fresh in the logs and the code around it has not changed. It also protects the people who rarely complain. For every user who writes in about a broken checkout step or a failing import, others simply leave.

## How fixing bugs affects retention and support load

Reliability is a feature that customers notice only when it is missing. When login errors, wrong totals, broken exports and stuck forms disappear, trial users reach the point where your product is useful. Existing customers stop opening tickets about the same problems, so your support queue gets shorter and your team gets time back.

The mechanism is simple. Each bug adds friction to a task the user came to do. Remove the friction and more people finish the task, return to it and recommend it. Fixes also give your developers confidence to change nearby code, which speeds up everything built afterwards.

## What a good bug fix includes

- A written reproduction: the exact steps, data and environment that trigger the problem.
- The root cause, not just the symptom, explained in plain language.
- A small, focused change in its own branch and merge request.
- A regression test, where the code allows it, so the same bug is caught if it returns.
- A check of nearby code that could fail in the same way.
- A staging check before anything reaches production.
- A short note for your support team explaining what changed.
- A clear verdict when the bug is really a design problem that needs a larger change.

## How we work

You send a list of bugs with screenshots, error messages, steps or links to existing tickets. We read each report, ask only the questions we need and agree a priority order with you. Then we work through the list one bug at a time: reproduce, find the cause, fix, test, and send you an update.

The Basic package covers a small set of bugs with a cause note for each. Standard adds more bugs, regression tests for the key fixes and a staging check before release. Premium adds a review of your error logs for repeat issues, tests for all fixes, a production release with notes and a prevention checklist for your team.

If a bug cannot be reproduced, we tell you what we tried and what extra information would help, rather than guessing. If it points to a deeper design flaw, we explain the options instead of hiding it under a patch.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe what you expected as well as what happened.
- Include the browser, device, account type and time when you can.
- Send screenshots, screen recordings and error text.
- Tell us which bugs hurt customers most.
- Keep a staging copy available for testing.

**Avoid:**
- Bundling several different problems into one report.
- Asking for a quick patch on a bug you have not been able to describe.
- Editing the same files while we work, which creates merge conflicts.
- Skipping the staging check on risky fixes.
- Treating every bug as equally urgent.

## Who this is for

This service suits a small SaaS team whose developers are busy with new work and never get to the bug backlog. It suits a founder who inherited a codebase from a previous agency and is not sure what is broken. It also suits a company about to launch a campaign that wants known problems cleared first.

## What we need from you

Send your bug list, a short note on your tech stack and access to the repository as a collaborator or developer user. A staging environment and read access to your error logs help a lot. We never need your passwords, and we work in your own account so the code and the fixes stay yours.
